clues.clue: I lived before a great flood.
clues.concern: Weak and ambiguous: Enoch also lived before the flood (Genesis 5:21-24), as did Abraham's ancestors generally. Noah also lived through and after the flood (Genesis 9:28), so 'lived before' undersells him. Consider rewording, e.g., 'I was six hundred years old when the flood came.'

clues.clue: God told me to build with gopher wood.
My sons were Shem, Ham and Japheth.
I built the ark.
clues.concern: Accurate (see also Genesis 6:22), but it gives away the answer outright. Placing it last is fine for difficulty 1, and it largely duplicates clue 2.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 ('I lived before a great flood') also fits Enoch, who lived and was taken before the flood (Genesis 5:21-24).
notes: The answer Noah is correct, and the explanation accurately quotes Genesis 6:14 within the cited Genesis 6:13-14. Clues 2-4 uniquely identify Noah, so the item is not actually ambiguous, but clue 1 should be tightened. The hint 'Look in Genesis' fits every option (Enoch, Abraham and Lot all appear in Genesis), so it is unhelpful though harmless.

clues.clue: I was a Nazarite from birth.
clues.concern: KJV says 'from my mother's womb' (also Judges 13:5), which is even earlier than birth; the clue is still accurate.

clues.clue: I tore a young lion with my bare hands.
Delilah learned the secret of my strength.
I pulled down the house where the Philistines gathered.
clues.concern: KJV describes Samson grasping the pillars and bowing himself with all his might, after which the house fell. 'Pulled down' is a fair paraphrase.

notes: Samson is uniquely identified by every clue. None of Gideon, Saul or Jephthah fits any of them. The explanation accurately reflects Judges 16:30.

clues.clue: An angel found me threshing wheat by a winepress.
I tested God with a fleece.
My army was reduced to three hundred men.
We carried trumpets, pitchers and lamps.

notes: All four clues match Gideon in the KJV. In Judges 6:11, Gideon 'threshed wheat by the winepress' when the angel of the LORD came and sat under an oak, which fits clue 1. The 'fleece of wool' appears in Judges 6:37. The army was reduced to 300 in Judges 7:6-7. Trumpets, empty pitchers and lamps appear in Judges 7:16 and 7:20. None of the clues fits Joshua, Barak or Ehud. Joshua's trumpets at Jericho involved no pitchers or lamps and no 300-man army. The explanation quotes Judges 7:7 accurately.

clues.clue: I was a woman of Moab.
clues.concern: Ruth 1:4 names both Orpah and Ruth as women of Moab, so this clue alone also fits the distractor Orpah. Ruth 2:2 ('Ruth the Moabitess') would point uniquely to Ruth.

clues.clue: I told my mother-in-law: whither thou goest, I will go.
I gleaned in the fields of Boaz.
I became an ancestor of King David.
clues.concern: Rahab is also an ancestor of David (Matthew 1:5-6), so this clue alone also fits the distractor Rahab.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 (woman of Moab) also fits Orpah (Ruth 1:4). Clue 4 (ancestor of King David) also fits Rahab (Matthew 1:5-6). Clues 2 and 3 resolve the answer uniquely to Ruth.
notes: The answer Ruth is correct, and the explanation matches Ruth 1:16. Two clues individually overlap with distractors, though the full set is unambiguous. Consider citing 'Ruth the Moabitess' (Ruth 2:2) for clue 1. The hint 'books of history' is acceptable.

clues.clue: My mother Hannah prayed for me at Shiloh.
clues.concern: Hannah's prayer at Shiloh (1:3, 1:9) is described in 1:10-11, and the answer comes with Samuel's birth and naming in 1:20. Accurate.

clues.clue: As a boy I served Eli the priest.
clues.concern: KJV says he 'ministered unto the LORD before Eli' (also 2:11). That is close enough to 'served Eli.'

clues.clue: I heard the LORD call my name in the night.
clues.concern: Accurate. The call happens at night while Samuel is lying down (3:3-4), and 3:10 gives 'Samuel, Samuel.'

clues.clue: I anointed both Saul and David.
clues.concern: Accurate. Saul's anointing is in 1 Samuel 10:1, and David's is in 16:13.

notes: Eli was the priest whom Samuel served, not the boy himself. Nathan and Gad were prophets in David's time, and neither fits any clue. The hint 'books of history' is fine, since 1 Samuel is a history book. The explanation matches 1 Samuel 3:10.

clues.clue: I was a prophetess.
clues.concern: Also fits distractors Miriam (Exodus 15:20) and Huldah (2 Kings 22:14). Acceptable as an opening clue, since later clues narrow it to Deborah.

clues.clue: I judged Israel under a palm tree in mount Ephraim.
clues.concern: Slight paraphrase. The KJV says she 'dwelt under the palm tree' and Israel 'came up to her for judgment'. The meaning is faithful.

clues.clue: I summoned Barak to fight Sisera.
A song of mine is recorded in Judges 5.
clues.concern: The song is sung jointly by Deborah and Barak ('Then sang Deborah and Barak'), so 'of mine' slightly overstates sole ownership. Minor.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 (prophetess) also fits Miriam and Huldah. The remaining clues uniquely identify Deborah, so the item as a whole is unambiguous.
notes: The answer is correct and well supported by Judges 4:4-5. The explanation matches the cited text. Optionally reword clue 4 to 'I sang a song with Barak, recorded in Judges 5' to reflect Judges 5:1 precisely.

clues.clue: As a baby I was hidden in an ark of bulrushes.
I was raised in Pharaoh's household.
clues.concern: Exodus 2:10 says he became Pharaoh's daughter's son. Acts 7:21-22 adds that she nourished him as her own son. 'Pharaoh's household' is a fair summary. Joseph was set over Pharaoh's house as an adult (Genesis 41:40), but he was not raised there, so there is no real conflict.

clues.clue: I saw a bush burn without being consumed.
I led Israel out of Egypt.
clues.concern: Aaron is also described as sharing this leadership: 'by the hand of Moses and Aaron' (Psalm 77:20; Exodus 6:26-27). On its own, this clue partly fits the distractor Aaron. The earlier clues make the answer unambiguous.

distractor_conflict: Clue 4 could partially apply to Aaron (Psalm 77:20; Exodus 6:26), but clues 1-3 uniquely identify Moses.
notes: The answer is correct. The explanation accurately reflects Exodus 3:4. The reference label covers only clue 3, which is acceptable. Consider rewording clue 4 to 'God sent me to bring Israel out of Egypt' (Exodus 3:10) to reduce overlap with Aaron.

clues.clue: I was born holding my twin brother's heel.
I bought my brother's birthright with pottage.
clues.concern: Esau is the one who sold the birthright, and this event is also strongly associated with him. But the first-person 'bought' wording fits only Jacob, so this is minor.

clues.clue: I dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven.
God renamed me Israel.
clues.concern: The renaming is also restated by God in Genesis 35:10.

notes: All clues are accurate to the KJV and point uniquely to Jacob. The explanation quotes Genesis 32:28 accurately.

clues.clue: I was my father's favourite son.
clues.concern: Benjamin was also especially loved by Jacob (Genesis 44:20, 30), so this clue alone could loosely fit a distractor, though Genesis 37:3 explicitly says Israel loved Joseph more than all his children.

clues.clue: My brothers sold me into slavery.
clues.concern: Judah proposed the sale (Genesis 37:26-27), but he was one of the sellers, not the one sold. No real conflict.

clues.clue: I interpreted Pharaoh's dreams.
I was set over all the land of Egypt.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 could loosely suggest Benjamin, whom Jacob also especially loved (Genesis 44:20). The other clues uniquely identify Joseph.
notes: The answer is clearly correct and the explanation matches the KJV wording of Genesis 41:41. The word 'favourite' does not appear in the KJV, but it is a fair paraphrase of 'loved Joseph more than all his children.' Consider clarifying clue 1 with the coat of many colours to remove any ambiguity with Benjamin.

clues.clue: I was a cunning hunter.
clues.concern: Nimrod is also called 'a mighty hunter' (Genesis 10:9), so this opening clue loosely fits a distractor, though the KJV phrase 'cunning hunter' is used only of Esau.

clues.clue: I was born red and hairy.
I sold my birthright for a meal.
I am also called Edom.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 (hunter) loosely overlaps with Nimrod, 'a mighty hunter before the LORD' (Genesis 10:9). The wording 'cunning hunter' (Genesis 25:27) is specific to Esau, and the later clues are decisive.
notes: The answer Esau is correct, and the explanation matches Genesis 25:33. The meal was bread and pottage of lentiles (Genesis 25:34). The name Edom is also tied to Esau at Genesis 25:30 and 36:8. Consider rewording clue 1 to quote the KJV exactly as 'a cunning hunter, a man of the field' to reduce the overlap with Nimrod.

clues.clue: I was ploughing with twelve yoke of oxen when I was called.
clues.concern: Accurate. Minor: the KJV spells it 'plowing', and the text says 'he with the twelfth', meaning Elisha himself drove the twelfth yoke. This clue is in 1 Kings, not 2 Kings as the hint suggests.

clues.clue: I asked for a double portion of my master's spirit.
I took up the mantle that fell from Elijah.
I told Naaman to wash in the Jordan seven times.
clues.concern: Minor: Elisha did not tell Naaman in person. He 'sent a messenger unto him', so 'told' is slightly loose but acceptable. The messenger is unnamed and not identified as Gehazi, so the clue does not fit that distractor.

notes: The marked answer, Elisha, is correct and every clue uniquely identifies him. Elijah is excluded by clue 3 and by being the master. Gehazi and Obadiah fit none of the clues. The explanation slightly abridges 2 Kings 2:9 ('I pray thee, let a double portion of thy spirit be upon me') but is accurate. Consider tweaking the clue 4 wording to 'I sent word to Naaman' and the clue 1 spelling to 'plowing' to match the KJV. The hint 'Look in 2 Kings' is fine, though clue 1 comes from 1 Kings.

clues.clue: I was one of twelve men sent to spy out Canaan.
clues.concern: Also fits distractor Caleb (Numbers 13:6), though later clues disambiguate. In Numbers 13:8, 16 Joshua is listed as Oshea the son of Nun, renamed Jehoshua by Moses.

clues.clue: I succeeded Moses as leader.
The walls of Jericho fell when the people shouted.
clues.concern: This clue is not first-person and does not directly identify the speaker. It is better phrased as 'I led Israel at Jericho, where the walls fell when the people shouted' (Joshua 6:16).

clues.clue: I said: As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 also fits Caleb, who was one of the twelve spies (Numbers 13:6). The remaining clues uniquely identify Joshua.
notes: The answer is correct, and the explanation accurately quotes Joshua 24:15. The hint 'books of history' is acceptable, but clue 1 points to Numbers, which belongs to the Pentateuch. Consider rewording clue 3 into the first person.

clues.clue: My house was upon the town wall of Jericho.
I hid two Israelite spies.
clues.concern: Joshua 2:6 also describes her hiding them under the stalks of flax on the roof.

clues.clue: I let them down by a cord through a window.
A line of scarlet thread marked my home.
clues.concern: Joshua 2:21 records that she actually bound the scarlet line in the window.

notes: The answer Rahab is clearly correct. No clue fits Jael, Deborah, or Ruth. The explanation matches Joshua 2:18: 'thou shalt bind this line of scarlet thread in the window.' The ref_kjv excerpt is truncated but accurate.

clues.clue: I left Ur of the Chaldees.
clues.concern: Lot also left Ur of the Chaldees with Terah and Abram in this verse, so the clue alone also fits the distractor Lot. Genesis 15:7 is more specific to Abram: 'I am the LORD that brought thee out of Ur of the Chaldees.'

clues.clue: God changed my name.
clues.concern: This also fits the distractor Jacob, whose name God changed to Israel (Genesis 32:28; 35:10).

clues.clue: My wife laughed at God's promise of a son.
God tested me in the land of Moriah.
clues.concern: The KJV says 'tempt'; 'tested' is an acceptable modern gloss. Isaac was also present in Moriah, but the text says God tempted Abraham, so this is fine.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 (left Ur) also fits Lot (Genesis 11:31). Clue 2 (God changed my name) also fits Jacob (Genesis 32:28). Taken together, the clues uniquely identify Abraham.
notes: The answer Abraham is correct, and the explanation accurately reflects Genesis 22:1-2. The two opening clues are individually ambiguous with the distractors Lot and Jacob. Consider rewording clue 2 to 'God changed my name from Abram' and clue 1 to cite Genesis 15:7, or reorder the clues so the distinctive ones come first.

clues.clue: I was a Tishbite.
Ravens fed me by the brook Cherith.
I challenged the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel.
I went up by a whirlwind into heaven.
clues.concern: Elisha witnessed this event but did not ascend himself, so the clue does not truly fit him.

notes: All clues are directly supported by the KJV and uniquely identify Elijah. The explanation matches 1 Kings 17:6. The hint 'Look in 1 Kings' is fine, though the whirlwind clue comes from 2 Kings 2:11.

clues.clue: I was the youngest son of Jesse.
clues.concern: 1 Samuel 17:14 also states 'David was the youngest.' Note that 1 Chronicles 2:15 calls David the seventh son, while 1 Samuel 16:10-11 implies an eighth son. This does not affect the clue.

clues.clue: I played the harp for King Saul.
I defeated Goliath.
clues.concern: 2 Samuel 21:19 credits Elhanan with slaying 'the brother of Goliath' (italicized words in the KJV). None of the distractors defeated Goliath, so the clue is still sound.

clues.clue: I became king over Israel.
clues.concern: This also fits the distractors Saul (1 Samuel 11:15) and Solomon (1 Kings 1:39; 1 Kings 4:1). On its own the clue is not distinguishing, but the other clues settle the answer.

distractor_conflict: The clue 'I became king over Israel' also fits Saul and Solomon. The earlier clues uniquely identify David.
notes: The answer David is correct. The explanation accurately paraphrases 1 Samuel 16:23. The item is fine overall; the final clue is generic but acceptable.

clues.clue: My mother was Bathsheba.
I asked God for an understanding heart.
I built the temple in Jerusalem.
clues.concern: David prepared materials and plans (1 Chronicles 22, 28), but God forbade him to build it (1 Chronicles 22:8). The clue does not fit David.

clues.clue: I judged between two women who both claimed one baby.

notes: All clues are accurate and point uniquely to Solomon. Bathsheba is also named as Solomon's mother in 1 Kings 1:11. David was Bathsheba's husband, not her son. Rehoboam's mother was Naamah (1 Kings 14:21). Hezekiah's mother was Abi (2 Kings 18:2). The explanation quotes 1 Kings 3:12 accurately. The cited range 1 Kings 3:10-12 is appropriate.

clues.clue: I was of the tribe of Benjamin.
clues.concern: Jonathan, as Saul's son, was also a Benjamite, so this clue alone also fits a distractor; the later clues disambiguate.

clues.clue: From my shoulders upward I was higher than any of the people.
Samuel anointed me as Israel's first king.
clues.concern: The KJV text says Samuel anointed him 'captain over his inheritance'. 'First king' is a fair inference from the narrative (1 Samuel 10:24) but is not stated verbatim. Samuel also anointed David (1 Samuel 16:13), though 'first' excludes him.

clues.clue: I consulted a woman at Endor.
clues.concern: The KJV calls her 'a woman that hath a familiar spirit at Endor'. The clue's wording is accurate.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 (tribe of Benjamin) also fits Jonathan, but the remaining clues uniquely identify Saul.
notes: The answer and explanation match 1 Samuel 9:2. The item is sound overall. Optionally strengthen clue 3 by citing 1 Samuel 10:1 together with 10:24.

clues.clue: I was taken captive to Babylon as a young man.
clues.concern: KJV calls Daniel and his companions 'children' (Daniel 1:4), so 'young man' is a fair paraphrase. Ezekiel was also a captive in Babylon (Ezekiel 1:1-3), but his age is not stated, and the clue is resolved by the later clues.

clues.clue: I purposed not to defile myself with the king's meat.
I read the writing on the wall.
clues.concern: Daniel both read and interpreted the writing (Daniel 5:17), so the clue is accurate.

clues.clue: I was delivered from the den of lions.

notes: The answer and explanation match Daniel 6:23, and the KJV quote is accurate. The hint 'Look in the Major Prophets' does not separate Daniel from Ezekiel or Jeremiah, which are also Major Prophets. Daniel's placement among the Major Prophets follows the English Protestant canon. The hint is harmless but weak.

clues.clue: I was raised by my cousin Mordecai.
clues.concern: The KJV does not use the word 'cousin', but it says Esther was 'his uncle's daughter' whom Mordecai 'took for his own daughter', which makes her his cousin. The clue is accurate.

clues.clue: I became queen in Persia.
clues.concern: Vashti, one of the distractors, was also queen of Ahasuerus in Persia (Esther 1:9). This clue alone does not distinguish Esther from Vashti, though the other clues resolve it.

clues.clue: I said: If I perish, I perish.
The feast of Purim remembers my people's deliverance.

distractor_conflict: Clue 2 ('I became queen in Persia') also fits Vashti, who was queen before Esther (Esther 1:9-11). The other clues identify Esther uniquely.
notes: The answer is correct and the explanation matches Esther 4:16 in the KJV. Consider rewording clue 2 (for example, 'I became queen in Persia after Vashti was deposed') so that it does not also fit the Vashti distractor. The hint 'books of history' is consistent with the conventional grouping of Esther among the historical books.

clues.clue: I lived in Nazareth of Galilee.
The angel Gabriel was sent to me.
clues.concern: Gabriel also appeared to Zacharias (Elisabeth's husband) in Luke 1:19, but not to Elisabeth herself, so there is no real conflict.

clues.clue: I was espoused to Joseph.
I gave birth to Jesus in Bethlehem.

notes: All clues are accurate and uniquely identify Mary. The explanation matches Luke 1:26-27. The clues give the answer away immediately, which is fine for difficulty 1.

clues.clue: I was cupbearer to King Artaxerxes.
clues.concern: Nehemiah 1:11 says 'For I was the king's cupbearer,' and Nehemiah 2:1 names the king as Artaxerxes. Neither verse alone covers the whole clue.

clues.clue: I wept over Jerusalem's broken walls.
clues.concern: Nehemiah wept after hearing the report of the broken wall while he was in Shushan. He was not looking at the walls, so 'wept over' is fine as an idiom but slightly loose.

clues.clue: I led the rebuilding of the city wall.
The wall was finished in fifty-two days.

notes: Ezra also served under Artaxerxes (Ezra 7), but he was a scribe, not the cupbearer. Ezra also wept, but over the people's sin (Ezra 10:1), not the walls. Zerubbabel and Haggai are tied to rebuilding the temple, not the wall. No clue fits a distractor. The explanation quotes Nehemiah 6:15 accurately, with an ellipsis.

clues.clue: I was a prophet, the son of Amittai.
clues.concern: Jonah 1:1 names him as the son of Amittai but does not use the word 'prophet'. 2 Kings 14:25 explicitly calls him 'the prophet'. Either reference supports the clue.

clues.clue: I fled from God's call on a ship.
I spent three days inside a great fish.
clues.concern: KJV says 'three days and three nights'. The clue is a fair simplification.

clues.clue: I was displeased when Nineveh repented.
clues.concern: Strictly, Jonah 4:1 follows God's sparing of the city (Jonah 3:10), which came after Nineveh repented. The clue is accurate in substance.

notes: The answer and the explanation are correct and match Jonah 1:1 verbatim. Nahum also prophesied concerning Nineveh, but none of the clues fit him. The item is clear and suitable for difficulty 1.

clues.clue: God said He knew me before He formed me in the belly.
I protested that I was only a child.
I was let down into a dungeon full of mire.
clues.concern: KJV says the dungeon had 'no water, but mire' and he 'sunk in the mire'. 'Full of mire' is a fair paraphrase.

clues.clue: Baruch wrote my words on a roll.

notes: All clues uniquely fit Jeremiah. Daniel was cast into a lions' den, not a miry dungeon, so there is no conflict. The explanation quotes Jeremiah 1:5 accurately and correctly labels 'weeping prophet' as tradition. The hint 'Major Prophets' fits all four options, so it is weak but not wrong.

clues.clue: I saw the Lord high and lifted up in the year King Uzziah died.
A seraph touched my lips with a live coal.
clues.concern: KJV says 'one of the seraphims' laid the coal 'upon my mouth'. 'Lips' is a reasonable paraphrase, since verse 7 says 'this hath touched thy lips'.

clues.clue: I answered: Here am I; send me.
I prophesied of a child called Immanuel.

notes: All clues are accurate and uniquely point to Isaiah. Jeremiah's mouth was touched by the LORD's hand (Jeremiah 1:9), not by a seraph with a coal. Ezekiel's throne vision (Ezekiel 1) lacks the Uzziah dating. Micah's Bethlehem prophecy (Micah 5:2) does not use the name Immanuel. The hint 'Major Prophets' also fits Jeremiah and Ezekiel, but the clues disambiguate. The explanation quotes Isaiah 6:8 correctly.

clues.clue: I was chief among the publicans.
clues.concern: Matthew was also a publican (Matthew 10:3), but only Zacchaeus is called 'chief among the publicans,' so the clue still points uniquely to him.

clues.clue: I was rich.
clues.concern: On its own this clue is weak, since Nicodemus could arguably be inferred as wealthy from John 19:39. It is acceptable in combination with the other clues.

clues.clue: I was little of stature.
I climbed a sycomore tree to see Jesus.

notes: All clues are accurately supported by Luke 19:2-4, and the KJV spelling 'sycomore' matches the text. The answer is unambiguous.

clues.clue: I was a fisherman, the brother of Andrew.
Jesus called me to become a fisher of men.
clues.concern: The call 'I will make you fishers of men' was addressed to both Peter and Andrew (and Mark 1:17 likewise), so on its own this clue also fits the distractor Andrew; combined with the other clues it is still unambiguous.

clues.clue: I walked on the water toward Jesus.
I denied Jesus three times before the cock crew.
clues.concern: Matthew 26:69-74 narrates the three denials themselves; verse 75 records Peter remembering Jesus' prediction. Both support the clue.

distractor_conflict: Clue 2 (fisher of men) also applies to Andrew per Matthew 4:19 and Mark 1:17, and arguably to James and John as fishermen called in the same scene, though only Peter and Andrew are told 'fishers of men'. The other clues uniquely identify Peter.
notes: The answer Peter is correct. The KJV quote of Matthew 26:75 is accurate, and the explanation's quotation matches the verse. Consider rewording clue 2 to be Peter-specific, for example using Luke 5:10, 'from henceforth thou shalt catch men', spoken to Simon. Alternatively, accept it because the clues are cumulative.

clues.clue: My father Zacharias was a priest.
clues.concern: Luke 1:5 identifies Zacharias as a priest. Luke 1:13 and 1:57-63 confirm that John was his son.

clues.clue: I wore raiment of camel's hair.
clues.concern: Elijah is described in 2 Kings 1:8 as 'an hairy man' girt with leather, which some read as a hair garment. The specific phrase 'camel's hair' applies only to John, so this is a minor overlap, not a real conflict.

clues.clue: I ate locusts and wild honey.
I baptized Jesus in the Jordan.

notes: The item is accurate and the clues together point only to John the Baptist. The explanation matches the cited verse, Matthew 3:4. Elijah is a reasonable thematic distractor because of 2 Kings 1:8 and Malachi 4:5 / Matthew 11:14, but no clue fully fits him. The baptism clue could also cite Matthew 3:13-16.

clues.clue: I was one of the twelve, called Didymus.
I was absent when Jesus first appeared to the disciples.
clues.concern: Minor imprecision: by Luke 24:34 and 24:13-31, Jesus had already appeared to Simon and to the two on the Emmaus road before the gathered disciples. 'First appeared to the disciples' fits the first-day evening appearance to the assembled disciples (John 20:19). Wording such as 'when Jesus came to the disciples on the first day of the week' would be more precise.

clues.clue: I wanted to see the print of the nails.
I said: My Lord and my God.

notes: All clues point uniquely to Thomas. Philip, Bartholomew and Matthew are not called Didymus, and none fits the other clues. The explanation matches John 20:28 in the KJV. Only a minor wording nuance in clue 2.

clues.clue: I lived in Bethany.
clues.concern: Simon the leper also lived in Bethany (Matthew 26:6; Mark 14:3), so this clue alone fits the distractor 'Simon'. The later clues disambiguate.

clues.clue: My sisters were Mary and Martha.
Jesus wept near my grave.
clues.concern: Slightly loose: Jesus wept after asking 'Where have ye laid him?' (John 11:34-35), on the way to the grave, before he came to it (John 11:38). Acceptable paraphrase.

clues.clue: Jesus called me out of the tomb.

distractor_conflict: The first clue (Bethany) also fits Simon the leper of Bethany (Matthew 26:6; Mark 14:3). The remaining clues uniquely identify Lazarus.
notes: The answer and the explanation match John 11:43 exactly. Minor issues: the Bethany clue overlaps with Simon the leper, and 'near my grave' is slightly imprecise per John 11:34-38. These are acceptable for a difficulty-1 item.

clues.clue: I was a Pharisee and a ruler of the Jews.
clues.concern: Gamaliel was also a Pharisee (Acts 5:34), and Joseph of Arimathaea was an 'honourable counsellor' (Mark 15:43). Neither is called 'a ruler of the Jews' in the KJV, so the combined clue still points uniquely to Nicodemus.

clues.clue: I came to Jesus by night.
Jesus told me I must be born again.
I brought myrrh and aloes for Jesus' burial.
clues.concern: Joseph of Arimathaea also took part in the burial (John 19:38-40). However, Scripture credits the myrrh and aloes specifically to Nicodemus, so the clue is accurate.

notes: The answer is correct and the clues are accurate. The explanation's quotation matches John 3:3 in the KJV. Clue 3 uses the wording 'must be born again', which is closest to John 3:7 ('Ye must be born again'); the reference_label could be broadened to include it, e.g. John 3:1-7. Clue 4 relies on John 19:39, which lies outside the cited range of John 3:1-3. The burial clue is the one most likely to make a player think of Joseph of Arimathaea, but it is textually specific to Nicodemus.

clues.clue: I was born in Tarsus.
I once persecuted the church.
A light from heaven blinded me near Damascus.
clues.concern: Acts 9:3-4 mentions the light but not the blindness. The blindness appears in Acts 9:8-9 and Acts 22:11 ('I could not see for the glory of that light').

clues.clue: I wrote many letters to the churches.
clues.concern: Scripture does not say 'many letters' in so many words. It is supported by the Pauline epistles addressed to churches (e.g., Romans 1:7, 1 Corinthians 1:2, 2 Thessalonians 3:17) and Peter's mention of 'all his epistles.'

notes: The answer Paul is correct. Barnabas was from Cyprus (Acts 4:36). Stephen was martyred. Silas did not persecute the church and was not converted near Damascus. Two small points: Acts 9:3-4 does not mention the blinding, so the reference could be widened to Acts 9:3-9. The explanation's statement 'He is later called Paul' is accurate per Acts 13:9, though that verse is not in the cited passage.

clues.clue: I lived in Bethany with my sister and brother.
clues.concern: Luke 10:38 says only 'a certain village'. Bethany and the brother Lazarus come from John 11:1, which is outside the cited reference.

clues.clue: I was cumbered about much serving.
Jesus said my sister had chosen the good part.
clues.concern: The KJV reads 'that good part', not 'the good part' (minor paraphrase). Verse 42 also falls outside the reference_label range of Luke 10:38-41.

clues.clue: I welcomed Jesus into my house.

notes: Martha is clearly correct, and none of the distractors (Mary Magdalene, Salome, Joanna) fits these clues. The explanation accurately quotes Luke 10:40. Consider extending reference_label to Luke 10:38-42 so it covers clue 3, and perhaps cite John 11:1 for the Bethany/brother detail.

clues.clue: I was one of seven chosen to serve the church.
clues.concern: Also fits the distractor Philip, who is named among the same seven in Acts 6:5. The text speaks of serving tables (Acts 6:2-3), which this clue paraphrases loosely as serving the church. It is acceptable only because later clues identify Stephen.

clues.clue: I was full of faith and power.
As I spoke I saw the heavens opened.
I was stoned while a young man named Saul watched.
clues.concern: Minor: the text says the witnesses laid their clothes at Saul's feet. Saul was consenting (Acts 8:1) and kept the raiment (Acts 22:20), so 'watched' is a reasonable inference.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 also fits Philip, who was one of the seven chosen in Acts 6:5.
notes: The answer Stephen is correct, and the explanation accurately summarizes Acts 7:58-59. Consider making clue 1 more specific or putting it last, since on its own it equally fits Philip.

clues.clue: I was a seller of purple.
I came from the city of Thyatira.
I heard Paul speak by a riverside at Philippi.
clues.concern: The riverside setting is in verse 13, not in the cited 16:14-15. Philippi is named in verse 12.

clues.clue: My household was baptized.
clues.concern: Household baptism also fits other figures, such as the Philippian jailer, Crispus and Stephanas, but none of these is among the options.

notes: The answer, Lydia, is correct and uniquely fits the clues. Dorcas, Priscilla and Phebe do not match any clue. The explanation is accurate but brief. The reference label could be widened to Acts 16:13-15 to cover the riverside detail.

clues.clue: I was a tiller of the ground.
God did not respect my offering.
I asked: Am I my brother's keeper?
God set a mark upon me.

notes: All clues match KJV Genesis 4 accurately. Abel was a keeper of sheep (Genesis 4:2), and his offering was respected (Genesis 4:4). Lamech references Cain's vengeance (Genesis 4:24) but none of the clues fit him. The explanation quotes Genesis 4:9 correctly.

clues.clue: My name is interpreted 'the son of consolation'.
clues.concern: Strictly, 'Barnabas' is the surname the apostles gave Joses; the interpretation applies to that surname. Minor wording issue only.

clues.clue: I sold land and laid the money at the apostles' feet.
I brought Saul to the apostles in Jerusalem.
I travelled with Paul on his first missionary journey.
clues.concern: Distractor Mark (John Mark) also went on the first journey as their minister (Acts 13:5) before leaving at Perga (Acts 13:13), so this clue alone partly fits Mark. 'First missionary journey' is a scholarly label, not a KJV term.

distractor_conflict: Clue 4 partially fits Mark, who accompanied Barnabas and Saul at the start of the first journey (Acts 13:5) before departing (Acts 13:13). The other clues uniquely identify Barnabas.
notes: Answer Barnabas is correct. Clues 1-3 point uniquely to Barnabas. Consider rewording clue 4, e.g. 'I was separated with Saul by the Holy Ghost for the work' (Acts 13:2), to avoid overlap with Mark. The explanation matches Acts 4:36.

clues.clue: I was formed of the dust of the ground.
I gave names to the animals.
I lived in the garden of Eden.
My wife was Eve.
clues.concern: Genesis 4:1 also explicitly calls Eve Adam's wife. Either verse supports the clue.

notes: Every clue is uniquely true of Adam. Cain and Seth were born after the expulsion from Eden (Genesis 4:1-2, 4:25). Enoch is a later descendant. The explanation quotes Genesis 2:20 accurately, and that verse falls within the cited range of Genesis 2:19-20.

clues.clue: My grandmother Lois and mother Eunice shared unfeigned faith.
I was Paul's young companion.
clues.concern: 'Companion' alone also fits Silas, Titus, and Luke. The word 'young' narrows it to Timothy (1 Timothy 4:12, 'thy youth'; Acts 16:1-3 tells how Paul took him along), but the clue is weak on its own.

clues.clue: Paul called me his dearly beloved son.
clues.concern: Titus is also called Paul's 'own son' (Titus 1:4), but only Timothy is called 'dearly beloved son,' so the wording still separates them.

clues.clue: Two New Testament letters are addressed to me.
clues.concern: The second letter is addressed to Timothy at 2 Timothy 1:2. Titus receives only one letter, so this clue does not fit him.

notes: The answer, Timothy, is correct. The cited reference (2 Timothy 1:2-5) supports clues 1, 3, and part of 4. Clue 2 is fairly generic, but the item as a whole is unambiguous.

clues.clue: I walked with God.
clues.concern: Also fits distractor Noah: 'Noah walked with God' (Genesis 6:9). Not unique on its own, though later clues disambiguate.

clues.clue: I was the father of Methuselah.
I was not, for God took me.
clues.concern: Loosely evocative of Elijah being taken up (2 Kings 2:11), but the 'he was not; for God took him' wording is unique to Enoch.

clues.clue: Hebrews says I was translated so I should not see death.
clues.concern: Accurate paraphrase. Elijah also escaped death (2 Kings 2:11), but Hebrews 11:5 names Enoch, so the clue is decisive.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 ('I walked with God') also fits Noah (Genesis 6:9). Clues 3–4 might bring Elijah to mind, since he was also taken without dying (2 Kings 2:11), but their specific wording points to Enoch.
notes: Answer Enoch is correct and well supported by Genesis 5:21-24 and Hebrews 11:5. The explanation quotes Genesis 5:24 accurately. Consider replacing or ordering clue 1 so the opening clue is not equally true of Noah, e.g. 'I walked with God three hundred years after begetting Methuselah' (Genesis 5:22). The hint 'Look in Genesis' is fine.

clues.clue: My father was Enoch.
My son was Lamech.
clues.concern: Another Lamech, of Cain's line, was the son of Methusael (Genesis 4:18). This does not conflict with any option.

clues.clue: I was Noah's grandfather.
clues.concern: This is inferred by combining Genesis 5:25 with 5:28-29. It is not stated in one verse, but the inference is sound.

clues.clue: I lived nine hundred sixty and nine years.

notes: No clue fits any distractor. Jared was Enoch's father (Genesis 5:18). Enoch's father was Jared (Genesis 5:18), and his son was Methuselah (Genesis 5:21). Mahalaleel's father was Cainan (Genesis 5:12), and his son was Jared (Genesis 5:15). The explanation quotes Genesis 5:27 accurately, though it omits the closing words 'and he died'.

clues.clue: I was king of Salem.
I was priest of the most high God.
I brought forth bread and wine to Abram.
clues.concern: The KJV says he 'brought forth bread and wine' without the words 'to Abram'. The recipient is clear from context (Genesis 14:17-19), so this is minor.

clues.clue: Abram gave me tithes of all.
clues.concern: Genesis 14:20 says only 'he gave him tithes of all', which is ambiguous about who gave to whom. Hebrews 7:2 and 7:4 state explicitly that Abraham gave Melchizedek a tenth of all, so Hebrews 7:2 is the clearer support.

notes: The answer is correct, and no distractor fits these clues. Jethro was a priest, but of Midian (Exodus 3:1), not king of Salem. Abimelech was king of Gerar. Aaron was a priest but not a king, and he lived long after Abram. The explanation matches Genesis 14:18. Consider adding Hebrews 7:1-2 as supporting text for the tithe clue. Difficulty 4 may be too high, since the first clue ('king of Salem') gives the answer away immediately.

clues.clue: My husband was Elkanah.
clues.concern: Also true of the distractor Peninnah, Elkanah's other wife (1 Samuel 1:2), so this clue does not distinguish the two on its own.

clues.clue: I prayed silently at Shiloh, and Eli thought I was drunk.
I vowed to give my son to the LORD.
I named my son Samuel.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 ('My husband was Elkanah') also fits Peninnah, Elkanah's other wife (1 Samuel 1:2). The later clues identify only Hannah.
notes: Hannah is the correct answer. The explanation matches 1 Samuel 1:20, which falls within the cited range 1:13-20. Shiloh as the setting is supported by 1 Samuel 1:3 and 1:9. Consider rewording clue 1 (e.g. 'My husband Elkanah had another wife who provoked me') so it no longer applies to Peninnah.

clues.clue: I lived in the land of Uz.
I was perfect and upright.
I lost my children and possessions in a single day.
clues.concern: The text does not say 'single day' outright, but the losses are reported in rapid succession ('While he was yet speaking') on the day his children were feasting (1:13). The clue is a fair summary.

clues.clue: I said: The LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away.

notes: All clues point uniquely to Job. Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite and Elihu the Buzite are never said to live in Uz, be called perfect and upright, or suffer these losses. The explanation quotes Job 1:21 accurately, and the hint is appropriate.

clues.clue: I was captain of the host of the king of Syria.
I was a leper.
clues.concern: On its own this also fits Gehazi, who was struck with Naaman's leprosy (2 Kings 5:27). The other clues make the answer unique.

clues.clue: A captive little maid from Israel told of a prophet.
clues.concern: The maid spoke to Naaman's wife (her mistress), not directly to Naaman. The clue's wording is acceptable but slightly loose.

clues.clue: I dipped myself seven times in the Jordan.

distractor_conflict: Gehazi also became a leper (2 Kings 5:27), so clue 2 alone fits him. The combined clues still point only to Naaman.
notes: The answer Naaman is well supported by 2 Kings 5:1-14. Ben-hadad was the king of Syria, not his captain. Hazael was a servant of Ben-hadad, not named as captain of the host. The explanation accurately paraphrases 2 Kings 5:14. It could add 'like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean' for completeness.

clues.clue: I was one of the twelve.
clues.concern: Also fits Peter, Thomas, and Andrew, but it is only a lead-in clue; the later clues are unique to Judas.

clues.clue: I had the bag.
I agreed to betray Jesus for thirty pieces of silver.
I betrayed Jesus with a kiss.

notes: The answer is correct, and the explanation matches Matthew 26:14-15. 'Had the bag' is in John 12:6 and John 13:29. The kiss is in Matthew 26:48-49 (also Mark 14:44-45 and Luke 22:47-48). Clue 1 is generic but harmless.

clues.clue: I was one of the twelve spies.
clues.concern: Also fits Joshua (Oshea son of Nun, Numbers 13:8), a listed option. Later clues resolve this.

clues.clue: I brought back a good report with Joshua.
clues.concern: The KJV never uses the phrase 'good report' (only 'evil report' for the others, Numbers 13:32), but the substance is supported. Numbers 13:30 and 14:7 ('exceeding good land') back it. The words 'with Joshua' rule out the Joshua option.

clues.clue: I was eighty-five years old when I asked for my inheritance.
I asked for the mountain and received Hebron.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 (one of the twelve spies) also fits Joshua. Clue 2 explicitly separates Caleb from Joshua, so the item is not ambiguous overall.
notes: The explanation matches Joshua 14:13: 'And Joshua blessed him, and gave unto Caleb the son of Jephunneh Hebron for an inheritance.' The reference label Joshua 14:6-13 covers clues 3 and 4. Clues 1 and 2 come from Numbers 13-14, which is Pentateuch rather than a 'book of history,' but the hint still points to the key passage in Joshua. A minor wording polish would be to say 'I gave a good report of the land' or to follow Numbers 14:7 more closely.

clues.clue: I was a publican.
clues.concern: This clue alone also fits Zacchaeus, who was 'chief among the publicans' (Luke 19:2).

clues.clue: I sat at the receipt of custom.
Jesus said to me: Follow me.
clues.concern: Jesus also said 'Follow me' to Simon Peter (Matthew 4:19), so this clue alone also fits Simon.

clues.clue: Jesus ate with publicans and sinners at my table.
clues.concern: Matthew 9:10 says only 'in the house' and does not name whose house. Luke 5:29 states the feast was in Levi's own house, which relies on identifying Levi with Matthew. Zacchaeus also hosted Jesus and was called a sinner (Luke 19:5-7), though that passage does not mention publicans and sinners eating together.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 (publican) also fits Zacchaeus (Luke 19:2), and clue 3 ('Follow me') also fits Simon (Matthew 4:19). Taken together, the clues point uniquely to Matthew.
notes: The answer is correct and the explanation matches Matthew 9:9. The clues would be stronger if clue 1 cited 'Matthew the publican' (Matthew 10:3). Clue 4 could be reworded to follow Matthew 9:10 ('as Jesus sat at meat in the house, many publicans and sinners came and sat down with him'), or cite Luke 5:29 and acknowledge that Levi is identified with Matthew.

clues.clue: I was a mighty man of wealth in Bethlehem.
clues.concern: Ruth 2:1 calls Boaz 'a mighty man of wealth' of Elimelech's family but does not name Bethlehem in that verse. His being of Bethlehem is supported by Ruth 2:4 ('Boaz came from Bethlehem').

clues.clue: I let a Moabite woman glean in my fields.
I redeemed the inheritance of Elimelech.
clues.concern: Minor: Boaz says he bought 'all that was Elimelech's' to 'raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance'. The wording 'redeemed the inheritance' is a fair paraphrase.

clues.clue: I married Ruth.
clues.concern: This clue gives the answer away outright.

notes: The answer and explanation are accurate. None of the distractors fits the clues: Elimelech was Naomi's husband and died, Obed was the son of Boaz, and Jesse was the grandson of Boaz.

clues.clue: I was a son of Zebedee.
clues.concern: Also fits James, a distractor; not distinguishing on its own.

clues.clue: Jesus surnamed my brother and me Boanerges.
clues.concern: Also fits James, since the name applied to both brothers.

clues.clue: Tradition identifies me as the disciple whom Jesus loved.
clues.concern: Explicitly labeled as tradition; Scripture never names the beloved disciple (John 21:20, 24). This is the first clue that separates John from James.

clues.clue: I was on the isle of Patmos for the word of God.
clues.concern: The text says 'I John' but does not state that this John is the son of Zebedee. Linking him to the apostle is traditional, and the explanation acknowledges this.

distractor_conflict: Clues 1 and 2 fit James equally well, because both sons of Zebedee were surnamed Boanerges. Only the traditional 'beloved disciple' clue and the Patmos clue, whose identification is also traditional, separate John from James.
notes: The answer John is defensible and the explanation accurately quotes Revelation 1:9 while noting the traditional identification. However, the distinguishing clues rest on tradition rather than explicit text. Consider adding a scripturally explicit distinguishing clue, for example: Peter and John were sent to prepare the passover (Luke 22:8), or Peter and John healed the lame man at the temple gate (Acts 3:1).

clues.clue: I was the first woman.
clues.concern: Not stated verbatim as 'first woman', but clearly implied by the creation account (Genesis 2:22-23; cf. 1 Timothy 2:13).

clues.clue: I was made from a rib taken from the man.
The serpent spoke to me in the garden.
I am called the mother of all living.

notes: All clues are well supported and uniquely fit Eve. Rachel, Hannah and Sarah do not fit any clue. The explanation accurately quotes Genesis 3:20 (KJV). Note that she is not named Eve until Genesis 3:20; in Genesis 2 she is called 'Woman' (Genesis 2:23), which is a minor point and does not affect the item.

clues.clue: My mother laughed when my birth was promised.
My father was a hundred years old when I was born.
I was laid on an altar in the land of Moriah.
clues.concern: Moriah is named in Genesis 22:2. Verse 9 records the laying on the altar.

clues.clue: My sons were Esau and Jacob.

notes: All clues point uniquely to Isaac. Ishmael's mother did not laugh, and Abraham was 86 at Ishmael's birth (Genesis 16:16). Jacob and Joseph do not fit. The explanation accurately paraphrases Genesis 22:9.

clues.clue: I watched over my baby brother at the river.
clues.concern: The sister in Exodus 2:4-8 is not named there. She is identified as Miriam only by inference from Numbers 26:59, where Miriam is the only sister of Moses and Aaron named.

clues.clue: I am called a prophetess.
clues.concern: Taken alone, this also fits the distractor Deborah, who is called a prophetess in Judges 4:4.

clues.clue: I led the women with a timbrel after the Red Sea crossing.
I was briefly struck with leprosy.
clues.concern: 'Briefly' is supported: she was shut out of the camp seven days (Numbers 12:14-15).

distractor_conflict: Deborah is also called a prophetess (Judges 4:4), so the second clue alone fits her. The other clues uniquely identify Miriam.
notes: The answer and the cited Exodus 15:20 are accurate. The first clue relies on identifying Moses' unnamed sister in Exodus 2 as Miriam. The hint 'Look in Exodus' fits the cited verse, though the leprosy clue comes from Numbers 12.

clues.clue: Seven devils had gone out of me.
clues.concern: Also stated in Mark 16:9. Unique to Mary Magdalene.

clues.clue: I stood by the cross.
clues.concern: Taken alone, this does not single her out. John 19:25 also places Mary the wife of Cleophas by the cross, and she is often identified with Mary the mother of James. Mark 15:40 and Matthew 27:55-56 show Mary the mother of James and Salome beholding from afar. The other clues resolve the ambiguity.

clues.clue: I came to the tomb while it was yet dark.
clues.concern: The other women, including Mary the mother of James and Salome, also came early (Mark 16:1-2; Luke 24:1, 10), but the wording 'yet dark' comes only from John 20:1, which names Mary Magdalene.

clues.clue: At first I supposed the risen Jesus was the gardener.

distractor_conflict: Clue 2 (standing by the cross) could loosely fit Mary the mother of James and Salome (John 19:25; Mark 15:40), but clues 1 and 4 are unique to Mary Magdalene, so the item as a whole is unambiguous.
notes: The answer, the reference (John 20:15-16) and the explanation are accurate to the KJV. Optionally, clue 2 could be made more distinctive, for example by echoing John 19:25 explicitly, although this is not necessary given the other clues.

clues.clue: I was Abram's nephew.
clues.concern: KJV never uses the word 'nephew' for Lot; it calls him 'Lot his brother's son' (Genesis 12:5; also Genesis 11:27, 31; 14:12). The meaning is accurate. Note that Genesis 13:8 and 14:14 call him Abram's 'brother' in the broader sense of kinsman.

clues.clue: I chose all the plain of Jordan.
Two angels came to my house in Sodom.
clues.concern: Genesis 19:1 says 'there came two angels to Sodom at even'. Verse 3 says they 'entered into his house'. The clue is accurate.

clues.clue: My wife looked back and became a pillar of salt.

notes: The answer is correct, and no distractor fits any of the clues. Terah was Abram's father. Nahor was Abram's brother, or his grandfather. Laban was the son of Bethuel and the grandson of Nahor, so he was Abram's grand-nephew rather than his nephew. The explanation accurately paraphrases Genesis 19:26. A minor wording point: the clue says 'nephew' while KJV says 'brother's son'. This is acceptable.

clues.clue: My father was Laban.
clues.concern: Also true of Leah, who is a distractor; the later clues make the answer clear, but this clue alone is not unique.

clues.clue: Jacob served seven years for me, and they seemed but a few days.
I was the mother of Joseph and Benjamin.
I died on the way to Bethlehem.
clues.concern: KJV says she 'was buried in the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem.' The clue is accurate. Genesis 35:16-18 also places her death on the road near Ephrath.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 (Laban as father) also fits Leah (Genesis 29:16). The other clues identify only Rachel.
notes: Rachel is the correct answer. The explanation accurately quotes Genesis 29:20, though it omits 'for the love he had to her'. Leah is excluded because Jacob served the first seven years for Rachel, not for Leah, even though he received Leah first. Consider making clue 1 more distinctive, e.g. 'I was Laban's younger daughter' (Genesis 29:16).

clues.clue: I was a priest of Midian.
I was Moses' father-in-law.
Moses kept my flock near Horeb.
I advised Moses to appoint rulers to judge the people.

notes: All clues are well supported. Laban was Jacob's father-in-law, not Moses', so he does not fit. Minor point: Moses' father-in-law is also called Reuel in Exodus 2:18 and Raguel in Numbers 10:29, but Jethro is the only name among the options, so there is no ambiguity.

clues.clue: I drew water for a stranger's camels at a well.
clues.concern: Rachel also met a stranger (Jacob) at a well, but there Jacob watered her flock (Genesis 29:10); there were no camels. This is not a real conflict.

clues.clue: I was the sister of Laban.
clues.concern: Rachel and Leah were Laban's daughters, not his sisters, so the clue points only to Rebekah.

clues.clue: I married Isaac.
I helped my son Jacob receive his father's blessing.

notes: All clues are accurate and uniquely identify Rebekah. The explanation accurately reflects Genesis 24:67.

clues.clue: I am called a soothsayer.
Balak, king of Moab, sent for me to curse Israel.
An angel with a drawn sword stood in my way.
clues.concern: Numbers 22:23 also describes the angel with a drawn sword, but there the ass sees him. Balaam himself sees the angel standing in the way with the sword drawn only in Numbers 22:31. Both verses support the clue.

clues.clue: My ass spoke to me.

notes: All of the clues fit Balaam. Balak is the one who sent for him, not the one sent for. Jethro and Korah do not fit any clue. The explanation accurately abridges Numbers 22:28. The 'soothsayer' clue comes from Joshua 13:22, not Numbers, but the hint 'Look in Numbers' still works for the item as a whole.

clues.clue: I was a Levite and the brother of Moses.
I spoke to Pharaoh on Moses' behalf.
I made a golden calf when the people asked.
My rod budded and yielded almonds.

notes: All clues are directly supported by the KJV text. Exodus 4:14 calls Aaron 'the Levite thy brother'. Exodus 7:2 says Aaron would speak unto Pharaoh. Exodus 32:1-4 records the people's request and Aaron fashioning the calf. Numbers 17:8 matches the quoted text and the explanation. Moses is also a Levite but cannot be his own brother, so no distractor fits all clues. Eleazar is Aaron's son and Joshua is an Ephraimite, so neither fits.

clues.clue: I was the wife of Uriah the Hittite.
King David saw me washing as he walked on his roof.
clues.concern: Minor: the KJV says David walked upon the roof of the king's house and saw a woman washing herself, so she was seen from the roof, not on it. The clue's wording is accurate.

clues.clue: I became the mother of Solomon.
My son King Solomon set a seat for me at his right hand.

notes: All clues uniquely identify Bathsheba. Michal was Saul's daughter and David's wife. Tamar was David's daughter, or Judah's daughter-in-law. Abigail was Nabal's widow. None of these fit the clues. The explanation matches 2 Samuel 11:3. The KJV spells the name 'Bath-sheba'.

clues.clue: I was the son of King Saul.
clues.concern: Also fits the distractor Ishbosheth, who was Saul's son (2 Samuel 2:8). The later clues settle it.

clues.clue: I climbed up to a Philistine garrison with my armourbearer.
My soul was knit with the soul of David.
I warned David by shooting arrows.
clues.concern: The arrows were a prearranged signal (1 Samuel 20:20-22). 'Warned' is a fair summary.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 (son of King Saul) also fits Ishbosheth (2 Samuel 2:8), but the other clues uniquely identify Jonathan.
notes: The answer is correct, and the explanation matches 1 Samuel 18:1. Making the first clue more specific would keep it from also fitting Ishbosheth. The clues as a set are unambiguous.

clues.clue: I was a champion of the Philistines.
I came from Gath.
clues.concern: On its own this also fits the distractor Achish, king of Gath (1 Samuel 21:10; 27:2). The other clues still make the answer unique.

clues.clue: My height was six cubits and a span.
A shepherd boy struck me down with a sling and a stone.
clues.concern: 'Shepherd boy' is a fair paraphrase. David kept his father's sheep (1 Samuel 17:15, 34) and was 'but a youth' (1 Samuel 17:42). The stone felled Goliath, and David then killed him with Goliath's own sword (1 Samuel 17:51). 'Struck me down' is still accurate.

distractor_conflict: Achish was also 'of Gath' (king of Gath, 1 Samuel 21:10; 27:2), so clue 2 alone fits him. The other clues rule him out.
notes: The answer is clearly Goliath. Clues 1-3 are all supported by 1 Samuel 17:4, and clue 4 by 1 Samuel 17:49-50. The explanation matches the cited verse. Og (Deuteronomy 3:11) is a giant but not a Philistine. Sisera was a Canaanite captain killed by Jael (Judges 4:21). The only minor overlap is clue 2 with Achish, which is acceptable given the combination of clues.

clues.clue: I was a prophet in David's court.
clues.concern: Also fits Gad, 'the prophet Gad, David's seer' (2 Samuel 24:11; 1 Samuel 22:5). Later clues disambiguate, so this is acceptable as an opening clue.

clues.clue: I told David his son would build God's house.
I told David a parable about a poor man's ewe lamb.
I said to David, Thou art the man.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 also fits Gad, David's seer and prophet (2 Samuel 24:11). Clues 2-4 apply only to Nathan.
notes: The answer and explanation are accurate to 2 Samuel 12:7. The first clue is non-unique, which is expected in a progressive 'Who am I?' format. The hint is valid, since 2 Samuel is a history book.

clues.clue: I was a priest at Shiloh.
clues.concern: Samuel also ministered before the LORD at Shiloh wearing a linen ephod (1 Samuel 2:18; 3:21), so this clue alone could loosely suggest Samuel. The later clues resolve this.

clues.clue: I thought Hannah was drunken as she prayed.
My sons Hophni and Phinehas were wicked.
clues.concern: The sons are named in 1 Samuel 1:3. Verse 2:12 calls them 'sons of Belial'; 'wicked' is a fair paraphrase.

clues.clue: I fell backward and died when I heard the ark was taken.
clues.concern: The text specifies that he fell from off the seat backward and his neck broke. The clue is accurate in substance.

notes: The answer Eli is clearly correct. The clues about Hannah, his sons, and his death uniquely identify him. The explanation matches 1 Samuel 4:18. The hint 'books of history' is appropriate for 1 Samuel.

clues.clue: I was a son of King David.
clues.concern: Fits all four options (Amnon, Adonijah and Solomon are also David's sons). This is acceptable as an opening clue but does not distinguish.

clues.clue: I stole the hearts of the men of Israel.
I led a rebellion against my father.
clues.concern: Could loosely fit Adonijah, who exalted himself to be king while David still lived (1 Kings 1:5). That was more a bid for the succession than an armed revolt against David, so it is only a minor overlap.

clues.clue: My head caught in an oak as my mule went on.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 fits every option. Clue 3 could arguably be applied to Adonijah (1 Kings 1:5), though clues 2 and 4 uniquely identify Absalom.
notes: The answer is correct and the explanation accurately matches 2 Samuel 18:9. Possible improvement: make clue 1 more specific, e.g. 'my mother was Maacah' (2 Samuel 3:3).

clues.clue: I was the daughter of the king of the Zidonians.
I was the wife of King Ahab.
I threatened Elijah's life after Mount Carmel.
I arranged Naboth's death to take his vineyard.

notes: All clues are accurate for Jezebel. 1 Kings 16:31 names her as the daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Zidonians, and as Ahab's wife. 1 Kings 19:2 matches the quoted KJV text. In 1 Kings 21, she writes letters in Ahab's name arranging false witnesses against Naboth. Athaliah is Ahab's daughter, not his wife (2 Kings 8:18, 26), so no clue fits her. Delilah and Vashti do not fit any clue.

clues.clue: I was a king of Judah.
clues.concern: Generic; fits all four options (Josiah, Manasseh, Uzziah were also kings of Judah), but later clues disambiguate.

clues.clue: I broke in pieces the brasen serpent that Moses had made.
Isaiah told me to set my house in order.
clues.concern: Also in 2 Kings 20:1.

clues.clue: God added fifteen years to my life.
clues.concern: Also in 2 Kings 20:6.

notes: Item is accurate. The first clue applies to every option, so it gives no help on its own. The other three clues apply uniquely to Hezekiah. The explanation quotes Isaiah 38:5 accurately. The hint 'Look in Isaiah' is valid, although the same events also appear in 2 Kings 18-20.

clues.clue: I became king of Judah at eight years old.
The book of the law was found in the temple in my reign.
I rent my clothes when it was read to me.
I kept a great passover.
clues.concern: On its own this also fits Hezekiah, who kept a great passover (2 Chronicles 30:1-26, especially v.26). The other clues identify Josiah, so the item is still answerable.

distractor_conflict: Clue 4 (a great passover) also fits Hezekiah (2 Chronicles 30). Clue 1 does not fit Joash, who was seven (2 Kings 11:21). Clues 1-3 uniquely identify Josiah.
notes: The answer and the explanation match 2 Kings 22:1. Consider sharpening clue 4 to make it unique to Josiah, e.g. 'no such passover since the days of the judges' (2 Kings 23:22). Alternatively, rely on the first three clues. 2 Chronicles 36:9 says Jehoiachin was eight, but he is not among the options.

clues.clue: I was a king of Israel.
clues.concern: Also true of every distractor (Jeroboam, Omri, Jehu were all kings of Israel). Acceptable as an opening clue, but it does not distinguish the answer by itself.

clues.clue: I married Jezebel.
I asked Elijah, Art thou he that troubleth Israel?
I wanted Naboth's vineyard for a garden of herbs.

distractor_conflict: Only clue 1 (king of Israel) also fits Jeroboam, Omri, and Jehu. The later clues uniquely identify Ahab.
notes: The item is accurate. Clues 2–4 match the KJV wording and identify Ahab uniquely. The explanation correctly quotes 1 Kings 21:2. The generic first clue is acceptable for a progressive 'Who am I?' format.

clues.clue: I was a priest of the course of Abia.
An angel appeared to me by the altar of incense.
clues.concern: KJV says the angel stood 'on the right side of the altar of incense'; 'by the altar' is a fair paraphrase.

clues.clue: I was struck dumb because I did not believe.
I wrote: His name is John.

notes: All clues are accurate to KJV Luke 1 and point uniquely to Zacharias. Joseph, Annas (a high priest, not of the course of Abia), and Simeon do not fit any clue.

clues.clue: I was a priest among the captives by the river Chebar.
I saw wheels whose rings were full of eyes.
I lay on my side for many days as a sign.
I prophesied to a valley of dry bones.

notes: All clues are accurate to the KJV and point only to Ezekiel. Ezekiel 1:1 places Ezekiel 'among the captives by the river of Chebar,' and 1:3 names him as 'the priest.' Ezekiel 1:18 says the rings 'were full of eyes.' Ezekiel 4:4-6 records him lying on his left side 390 days and on his right side 40 days. Ezekiel 37:1-4 is the valley of dry bones. Jeremiah was also a priest's son (Jeremiah 1:1), but he was not at Chebar. None of the clues fit Daniel or Zechariah. The explanation quotes Ezekiel 37:4 accurately, and the hint pointing to the Major Prophets is fine.

clues.clue: I was among the herdmen of Tekoa.
I was a gatherer of sycomore fruit.
I said I was no prophet, neither a prophet's son.
I cried: let judgment run down as waters.
clues.concern: Minor: KJV reads "let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream." The clue is a faithful partial quote.

notes: All clues are uniquely Amos. Micah was a Morasthite (Micah 1:1), so none of the clues fit Micah, Obadiah or Hosea. The explanation accurately abridges Amos 7:14. The KJV of Amos 1:1 reads "among the herdmen of Tekoa," which matches clue 1.

clues.clue: I was a prophet to Israel.
clues.concern: Generic; Amos was also a prophet to (northern) Israel (Amos 7:15), so this clue alone fits a distractor, though later clues disambiguate.

clues.clue: I obeyed God and took Gomer as my wife.
I named a son Loammi.
clues.concern: God commanded the name ('Call his name Loammi'). The text does not explicitly say Hosea performed the naming, though that is implied.

clues.clue: I bought a woman for fifteen pieces of silver and barley.
clues.concern: Slightly imprecise. KJV specifies 'an homer of barley, and an half homer of barley.' The text does not explicitly name the woman as Gomer, which is fine since the clue says 'a woman.'

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 (prophet to Israel) also fits Amos, and arguably Micah, who prophesied concerning Samaria. It is resolved by the other clues.
notes: The answer and explanation match Hosea 1:3. Consider making clue 1 more specific, e.g. 'I prophesied in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash and Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah.' Even that partially overlaps with Amos, so a stronger unique detail would work better.

clues.clue: I was a priest and a ready scribe in the law of Moses.
clues.concern: Ezra 7:6 gives 'ready scribe in the law of Moses'. The priestly title appears in Ezra 7:11 ('Ezra the priest, the scribe') and in the lineage of 7:1-5.

clues.clue: I went up from Babylon in the reign of Artaxerxes.
clues.concern: Nehemiah also went up in Artaxerxes' reign (Nehemiah 2:1-11), though from Shushan. Nehemiah 13:6-7 calls Artaxerxes 'king of Babylon' when Nehemiah returned to Jerusalem. This adds slight overlap with a distractor, but the other clues disambiguate.

clues.clue: I read the book of the law to the people.
I stood upon a pulpit of wood.

distractor_conflict: Clue 2 partially fits Nehemiah, who also went to Jerusalem in Artaxerxes' reign (Nehemiah 2:1; 13:6-7). Taken together, the clues point uniquely to Ezra.
notes: The item is accurate. Consider citing Ezra 7:6 and Ezra 7:11 for the first clue. The explanation matches Nehemiah 8:4.

clues.clue: I was of the daughters of Aaron.
I was barren and well stricken in years.
clues.concern: Luke 1:7 says 'they both were now well stricken in years', referring to Zacharias and Elisabeth together; the barrenness is Elisabeth's. The clue is accurate. 'Barren' alone could loosely evoke Sarah, Hannah, or Rachel, but none of them is among the options.

clues.clue: My babe leaped in my womb when Mary greeted me.
I was the mother of John the Baptist.
clues.concern: The KJV does not use the exact phrase 'mother of John the Baptist' for Elisabeth. It is clearly implied: she bore a son and insisted he be called John (Luke 1:57-60), and that John is identified as the Baptist (Luke 3:2-3; Matthew 3:1). The clue also gives the answer away completely.

notes: Accurate item. Anna (Luke 2:36) was of the tribe of Aser, not Aaron. Salome and Mary do not fit the clues. The last clue is a near-giveaway, which is acceptable for difficulty 2. The explanation matches Luke 1:41.

clues.clue: I was a just and devout man in Jerusalem.
clues.concern: 'Just' alone could loosely evoke Joseph of Arimathaea (Luke 23:50, 'a good man, and a just') or Zacharias (Luke 1:6, 'righteous'), but 'just and devout' in Jerusalem matches Luke 2:25 exactly. This is minor, and later clues disambiguate.

clues.clue: The Holy Ghost revealed I would not die before seeing the Lord's Christ.
I took the child Jesus up in my arms in the temple.
I said: Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace.

notes: Accurate item. The quote matches the KJV of Luke 2:29 exactly. The distractors are plausible but are excluded by clues 2-4.

clues.clue: I was of the house and lineage of David.
An angel told me in a dream not to fear to take Mary as my wife.
I took the young child and his mother into Egypt by night.
People called Jesus the carpenter's son.
clues.concern: The clue is phrased in the first person but describes what people said about Jesus. It is accurate, though slightly awkward; 'People called Jesus my son, the carpenter's son' might read better.

notes: The answer is correct, and the explanation quotes Matthew 1:20 accurately. No distractor fits any clue. Joseph of Arimathaea is not said to be of David's line or a carpenter, and Zacharias and Simeon do not fit either. One small point: Luke 2:4 says 'of the house and lineage of David' verbatim, whereas Matthew 1:20 only says 'son of David.' The hint 'Look in Matthew' still works, since Matthew 1:20 supports the Davidic descent.

clues.clue: I was a prophetess of the tribe of Aser.
I was a widow of about fourscore and four years.
clues.concern: The clue quotes the KJV wording exactly, so it is supported. The Greek and KJV phrasing is ambiguous: it may mean she was 84 years old or had been a widow for 84 years. This is not a problem for the quiz.

clues.clue: I served God with fastings and prayers night and day.
I gave thanks when the child Jesus was brought to the temple.
clues.concern: Luke 2:38 does not name the temple directly. It says she came 'in that instant', referring to the presentation described in Luke 2:22-27, where the parents brought in the child Jesus (2:27). The clue is accurate in context.

notes: Anna is clearly correct. None of the distractors fits any clue: Elisabeth (Luke 1), Phebe (Romans 16:1) and Dorcas (Acts 9:36) are all distinct women. The explanation accurately quotes Luke 2:36. You might extend the reference label to Luke 2:36-38, since clues 2-4 come from verses 37-38.

clues.clue: I was from Cana of Galilee.
I asked: Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth?
Jesus saw me under the fig tree.
Jesus called me an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile.

notes: All clues are accurate to the KJV. John 21:2 names 'Nathanael of Cana in Galilee'. Thomas is also named in John 21:2, but the text does not say he was from Cana, so the first clue does not fit him. Philip was from Bethsaida (John 1:44). The first clue is the weakest, since its support comes from John 21 rather than John 1, but it is correct. Clue order is reasonable, though the first clue alone may be somewhat obscure. The explanation quotes John 1:47 exactly.

clues.clue: I was from Bethsaida.
clues.concern: This also fits the distractor Philip. John 1:44 says 'Philip was of Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter,' so the clue alone does not separate Andrew from Philip.

clues.clue: I was one of two who heard John the Baptist speak and followed Jesus.
I brought my brother Simon to Jesus.
I told Jesus of a lad with five barley loaves.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 (from Bethsaida) also fits Philip, who is explicitly said to be of Bethsaida in John 1:44.
notes: The answer Andrew is correct. Clues 2-4 identify Andrew uniquely, so the full set still resolves to him. Clue 1 is weak because it applies equally to Philip, one of the options. Consider rewording it, e.g. 'My city, Bethsaida, was also Peter's,' or simply accept it as a non-unique opening clue. The explanation matches John 1:41-42.

clues.clue: I was high priest that same year.
clues.concern: Annas is also called high priest in Luke 3:2 and Acts 4:6, but 'that same year' is the Johannine phrase used of Caiaphas (John 11:49; 18:13), so the clue is acceptable.

clues.clue: I said it was expedient that one man should die for the people.
Annas was my father-in-law.
Annas sent Jesus to me bound.

notes: The answer, the reference text and the explanation are all accurate. The ref_kjv matches John 11:49-50. John 18:14 also recalls Caiaphas's counsel that it was expedient one man should die for the people. No distractor fits all the clues.

clues.clue: I lived in Joppa.
I was full of good works and almsdeeds.
I made coats and garments that the widows showed.
clues.concern: Slightly loose paraphrase: the widows showed the coats and garments that Dorcas made while she was with them. Accurate in substance.

clues.clue: Peter said to me, arise, and I opened my eyes.

notes: All clues are directly supported by Acts 9:36-40. None of them fits Lydia (Thyatira and Philippi, Acts 16:14), Priscilla (Acts 18), or Phebe (Cenchrea, Romans 16:1). The explanation accurately quotes Acts 9:40.

clues.clue: I was from Bethsaida.
clues.concern: Also fits the distractor Andrew. John 1:44 calls Bethsaida 'the city of Andrew and Peter', so this clue alone does not single out Philip.

clues.clue: Jesus said to me, Follow me.
clues.concern: Jesus said 'Follow me' to several people, including Andrew together with Peter in Matthew 4:19 ('Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men'). The clue is generic, though accurate for Philip.

clues.clue: I told Nathanael: Come and see.
I asked Jesus: Lord, shew us the Father.

distractor_conflict: Andrew fits clue 1 (Bethsaida, John 1:44) and arguably clue 2 (Matthew 4:19). Clues 3 and 4 identify only Philip, so the answer remains unambiguous overall.
notes: The answer Philip is correct, and the explanation quotes John 14:8 accurately. The early clues are weak discriminators because Andrew shares them. Consider replacing clue 1 or clue 2 with something unique to Philip, such as Jesus asking him where to buy bread (John 6:5) or the Greeks coming to him (John 12:21). Bartholomew is traditionally identified with Nathanael, but that does not create a conflict, since Nathanael is the person Philip spoke to.

clues.clue: I was a centurion of the Italian band.
I was a devout man who prayed to God alway.
An angel told me to send to Joppa for Peter.
The Holy Ghost fell on all who heard Peter speak in my house.
clues.concern: Acts 10:44 does not explicitly say 'in my house,' but the setting is established in Acts 10:24-27 and confirmed in Acts 11:12-15, so the clue is acceptable.

notes: All clues are uniquely true of Cornelius. Julius was a centurion of Augustus' band (Acts 27:1), not the Italian band. Claudius Lysias was a chief captain (Acts 23:26). Sergius Paulus was a deputy (proconsul) of Paphos (Acts 13:7). No distractor fits any clue. The explanation matches Acts 10:1.

clues.clue: I was the Roman governor of Judaea.
clues.concern: The KJV calls Pilate 'governor of Judaea' but does not use the word 'Roman'; that is implied by context (Tiberius Caesar). On its own, this clue also fits Felix, who was likewise a Roman governor (Acts 23:24-26; Acts 24:27).

clues.clue: My wife sent word about a dream concerning a just man.
I asked: What is truth?
I washed my hands before the multitude.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 alone also fits Felix, who was also a Roman governor in Judaea (Acts 23:24; Acts 24:27). Clues 2-4 are unique to Pilate, so the item as a whole is unambiguous.
notes: The answer is correct and the explanation matches Matthew 27:24. The first clue is generic, so it could say 'governor of Judaea in the days of Tiberius Caesar' to tie it to Pilate. Difficulty 1 is appropriate.

clues.clue: I was a Pharisee and a doctor of the law.
I was had in reputation among all the people.
I told the council to let the apostles alone.
Paul was brought up at my feet.

notes: All clues are accurately supported by the KJV. Acts 5:38 reads 'Refrain from these men, and let them alone.' Acts 22:3 reads 'brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel.' Nicodemus was also a Pharisee and a ruler, and Jesus called him 'a master of Israel' (John 3:1, 10), but he is never called a doctor of the law, and the remaining clues do not fit him. Caiaphas was high priest, not a Pharisee. Neither Ananias, whether the one in Acts 5 or the high priest in Acts 23, fits these clues. The first clue alone is weakly distinguishing, but together the clues are unambiguous. The explanation is accurate to Acts 5:34.

clues.clue: I was a chief man among the brethren.
clues.concern: Acts 15:22 calls both Judas surnamed Barsabas and Silas 'chief men among the brethren'; it fits Silas but not uniquely. No distractor fits it.

clues.clue: I travelled with Paul after he parted from Barnabas.
clues.concern: Timothy also joined Paul soon after the split (Acts 16:1-3), so this clue alone partly fits a distractor. Acts 15:40 explicitly names Silas as the one Paul chose.

clues.clue: I was beaten and put in the stocks with Paul at Philippi.
At midnight Paul and I prayed and sang praises.

distractor_conflict: Clue 2 could loosely fit Timothy, who joined Paul's company after the split with Barnabas (Acts 16:1-3). However, Silas is the one Paul chose to travel with (Acts 15:40), and clues 3-4 uniquely identify Silas.
notes: The answer Silas is correct and well supported. The explanation accurately quotes Acts 16:25 (KJV). Consider rewording clue 2 to 'Paul chose me to travel with him after he parted from Barnabas' to tie it to Acts 15:40 and exclude Timothy.

clues.clue: I was a Jew born at Alexandria.
I was an eloquent man, mighty in the scriptures.
Aquila and Priscilla taught me the way of God more perfectly.
clues.concern: The KJV order is 'Aquila and Priscilla' and the text says they 'expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly'. 'Taught' is a fair paraphrase. Because Aquila is named in this clue, it rules him out as the answer rather than creating a conflict.

clues.clue: Paul wrote that he planted and I watered.

notes: The item is accurate. No clue fits Titus, Silas or Aquila. The explanation matches Acts 18:24. The hint 'Look in Acts' is fine, though the final clue comes from 1 Corinthians.

clues.clue: My husband Aquila and I were tentmakers.
clues.concern: KJV says 'by their occupation they were tentmakers'; acceptable to include Priscilla.

clues.clue: We came from Italy when Claudius commanded the Jews to leave Rome.
Paul stayed and worked with us in Corinth.
We expounded the way of God more perfectly to Apollos.

notes: All clues are well supported by Acts 18:1-3, 26. No clue fits Dorcas, Lydia (a seller of purple), or Phebe. The explanation's 'took Apollos aside' paraphrases KJV 'took him unto them' and is acceptable. Optional: the explanation could also cite Acts 18:2-3 for the earlier clues.

clues.clue: I was king in Judaea when Jesus was born.
clues.concern: Matthew 2:1 says 'Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judaea in the days of Herod the king'; Luke 1:5 also calls him 'king of Judaea.' The clue is accurate.

clues.clue: I was troubled when wise men asked for the King of the Jews.
I told the wise men to bring me word again.
I ordered the children in Bethlehem slain.
clues.concern: The KJV says Herod 'sent forth, and slew all the children... from two years old and under,' including those 'in all the coasts thereof.' 'Ordered... slain' is a fair paraphrase.

notes: The answer Herod (Herod the Great) is correct. Archelaus appears only in Matthew 2:22, where he reigns after Herod's death, so he fits none of the clues. Pilate and Augustus do not fit the clues either. Augustus is linked to the birth narrative through his decree in Luke 2:1, but he was emperor, not king in Judaea. The explanation accurately reflects Matthew 2:16.

clues.clue: I was the wife of Heber the Kenite.
Sisera fled to my tent.
I gave him milk when he asked for water.
I drove a nail of the tent into his temples.

notes: All clues are accurate to the KJV text of Judges 4:17-21, and Judges 5:24-26 corroborates them. Deborah is in the same narrative, but none of the clues fit her. Rahab and Delilah do not match any clue. The difficulty rating of 4 may be high for such a well-known story, especially since the first clue already gives away the answer.

clues.clue: My husband Nabal was churlish.
I brought bread, wine and figs to David's men.
clues.concern: Accurate but partial: she also brought dressed sheep, parched corn and raisins. The gift was sent to David and intended for his young men (1 Samuel 25:27).

clues.clue: I persuaded David not to shed blood.
After Nabal died, I became David's wife.
clues.concern: Bathsheba also married David after her husband died, but naming Nabal makes the clue unique to Abigail. David's sending and wooing begins at 1 Samuel 25:39.

notes: The answer is clearly Abigail, and every clue is supported by 1 Samuel 25. The explanation accurately paraphrases 1 Samuel 25:3. Ahinoam appears in 1 Samuel 25:43 as another wife, but no clue fits her. Clue 1 alone names Nabal and gives the answer away, which is acceptable for difficulty 3.

clues.clue: I lived in the valley of Sorek.
The lords of the Philistines offered me silver.
I asked a strong man the secret of his strength.
I had his seven locks shaved while he slept.
clues.concern: Minor: KJV says she made him sleep upon her knees and called for a man who shaved off the seven locks. 'Had shaved' accurately reflects that she did not shave him herself.

notes: Accurate item. Judges 16:4 names Delilah in the valley of Sorek. Verse 5 has the lords' offer of eleven hundred pieces of silver each. Verse 6 has her question. Verse 19 has the shaving of the seven locks. None of the distractors fit: Jael killed Sisera with a tent nail while he slept, but she was not linked to Sorek, silver, or hair. The explanation's addition of 'Samson' is supported by the context.
